statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES / orange. Tail is elevated after a firm U.S. cash open, while verified post-open retracement evidence remains incomplete.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The active danger window is 13:30-15:30 UTC; persistence depends on post-open extension and retracement quality.
headline: Elevated Tail after a firm Nasdaq cash open
body: U.S. equities opened higher, with the Nasdaq Composite up 0.76% at the bell after an extended premarket Nasdaq-futures advance. The open preserved the bullish regime, but sufficiently granular evidence of repeated failed retracements after the bell is not yet verified. Lower oil and Treasury yields support technology risk appetite, while inflation and policy uncertainty keep Stress extreme.

lookbackSummary: Tail was low through most of Sunday and early Monday, moved to WATCH as NQ strengthened, and entered the elevated band before the U.S. cash session as repeated upside extension and near-high retention developed.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is 31% / elevated. The cash open confirmed a firm bullish setup, but the high-Tail branch still requires verified post-open directional efficiency with shallow or failed retracements. The base path de-escalates after the opening window if two-way price discovery develops.

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash session opened higher after an extended premarket advance. Tail is elevated because the opening gap preserved the bullish regime, but no verified post-open sequence yet establishes repeated failed retracements or a sustained no-retracement path.
drivers: Post-open retracement quality remains the key test
Lower oil and Treasury yields support technology risk appetite

forecast.analysis: 16 UTC: the base path steps down from the opening window. Tail remains elevated only if NQ holds near session extremes and fresh extension follows weak retracements; broader rotation would support normalization.
17 UTC: WATCH is the conditional base case if the morning advance stays intact but directional efficiency slows. Deeper retracement or wider two-way trade would weaken the one-way-path risk.
drivers: Opening-window risk should decay if retracements broaden

forecast.analysis: 18 UTC: absent renewed one-way extension, low Tail is the base case as the market moves into midday. Stress remains high because rates, inflation sensitivity and geopolitical headlines can still create large but recoverable moves.

19 UTC: power hour is a WATCH checkpoint only if a fresh session extreme is paired with shallow or failed retracements. Without that combination, the late-session structure remains more consistent with two-sided trade.
drivers: Fresh session extreme would matter only with weak retracements

forecast.analysis: 20 UTC: after the main U.S. session, low Tail is the base case unless the close develops unusually efficient directional continuation with little retracement.
21 UTC: the base case remains low Tail after the cash close. Residual Stress reflects policy and geopolitical uncertainty rather than an assumed one-way price path.
22 UTC: early after-hours conditions can be thinner, but low Tail remains the base case unless fresh headlines create persistent directional efficiency rather than a transient gap.
drivers: Persistence, not gap size, governs Tail

forecast.analysis: 23 UTC: low Tail remains conditional on ordinary two-way after-hours trade. A new geopolitical or policy shock would raise Stress first unless subsequent price action becomes persistently one-way.
drivers: Stress can rise without immediate Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: 00 UTC: with no scheduled high-impact U.S. release in this hour, low Tail is the base case. Any overnight gap would require follow-through and failed retracements before materially changing the path assessment.
drivers: No scheduled high-impact U.S. release in this hour

forecast.analysis: 01 UTC: low Tail remains the base case during quieter overnight trade. Thin liquidity may enlarge moves, but persistence and retracement failure would still be required for a higher Tail band.
02 UTC: the forecast remains low Tail absent a new directional catalyst. Cross-asset moves may change Stress, while Tail requires evidence that mean reversion is actually failing.
drivers: No scheduled U.S. catalyst in this hour
Cross-asset stress can diverge from Tail
Mean-reversion failure remains the key condition

forecast.analysis: 03 UTC: ordinary overnight consolidation is the base case. A material Asia-session extension would become relevant only if it holds near extremes and resists meaningful retracement.
04 UTC: low Tail remains the base case before Europe becomes more active. A fresh gap alone would not justify escalation without persistent follow-through.
drivers: No automatic Tail increase from volatility alone

forecast.analysis: 05 UTC: Europe begins to add liquidity. Tail stays low unless cross-market alignment accompanies sustained NQ extension and weak pullbacks rather than a reversible regional-open move.
06 UTC: the European morning can transmit rates and geopolitical news into U.S. futures. The base case remains low Tail unless those drivers align with persistent NQ structure.
drivers: Persistent NQ structure required for escalation

forecast.analysis: 07 UTC: low Tail remains the base case, with uncertainty gradually rising as U.S. participation approaches. Overnight extremes become relevant only if they are defended through repeated retracement attempts.
08 UTC: the forecast holds Tail at the top of the low band. A directional Europe-to-U.S. handoff with aligned technology leadership would increase risk, while rotation would keep the path contained.
09 UTC: low Tail remains conditional before the U.S. premarket deepens. Policy headlines may lift Stress, but the path requires sustained extension and weak retracements before Tail moves higher.

10 UTC: the base case remains low Tail, with attention shifting toward the next U.S. session. Overnight direction is not sufficient by itself; continuation quality will determine whether WATCH is justified.
drivers: Overnight direction is not sufficient alone

forecast.analysis: 11 UTC: WATCH is the conditional base case as U.S. participation increases and the market approaches the next cash-session setup. The score reflects uncertainty, not already-observed continuation.
drivers: Conditional WATCH rather than observed continuation

forecast.analysis: 12 UTC: WATCH persists ahead of the next U.S. open. A large premarket move would primarily raise Stress unless accompanied by repeated extension and shallow retracements.
drivers: Large moves primarily affect Stress without persistence

forecast.analysis: 13 UTC: the U.S. cash-open hour is a WATCH checkpoint. Tail would rise only if the opening auction produces persistent directional efficiency with weak retracements; two-way discovery would keep the score below the blocking threshold.
drivers: Two-way discovery is the main invalidation

forecastDetail.comment: The cash open confirmed a firm bullish setup, but verified post-open retracement evidence is still incomplete; Tail therefore remains elevated rather than high.
Elevated Tail persists conditionally if the first full cash-session hour extends with shallow pullbacks; substantive two-way rotation would de-escalate the path.
After the opening window, Tail falls unless NQ continues to hold near extremes and extend after weak retracements.
WATCH reflects residual trend persistence risk; broader two-way trade would support further normalization.
Low Tail is the midday base case absent renewed directional efficiency, while macro and geopolitical uncertainty keep Stress high.
Power hour returns to WATCH only if a fresh extreme is paired with shallow or failed retracements.
